Subject: SLO matrix & regional routing: post-demo next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation.  Quick recap and the immediate asks so we can size a focused POC: 

1) Targets you confirmed on the call
   - US: 95th pctl latency <= 180ms (99th ideally <= 300ms) for 1–2k RPS
   - EU: 95th pctl latency <= 220ms for 500–1k RPS
   - APAC: best-effort 95th pctl <= 350ms; goal for local-region residency

2) Throughput/concurrency and streaming
   - Steady concurrency target: ~200 concurrent sessions (chat-style) peak 600
   - Streaming: token-by-token low-latency streaming required for front-end UX (avg 40 tokens/sec per session)

3) Data residency constraints
   - EU customer data must remain in EU processing region (no egress to US for user prompts).
   - Billing/metadata may flow to US backend only after anonymization (you flagged legal review).

4) Next steps (action items)
   - Evelyn (me): share a performance-matrix.xlsx with recommended instance sizing, KV cache guidance, and routing policy options (attached).
   - Marcus / Karthik: quick capacity read on Dedicated vs. Hosted routing policy for the POC.
   - BrightCommerce: confirm anonymized sample traffic and a short test prompt set (2–3 days).

Please confirm the anonymized dataset access window and preferred POC kickoff week (we suggested Oct 5).  I attached a draft performance matrix and our SOC2 questionnaire you asked for.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Thanks, Evelyn — very clear recap. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming: when you say avg 40 tokens/sec per session, is that per connection after warm start (we typically see bursts on first response). We need to know recommended token throughput for warm vs cold.
- Concurrency: the 200 steady / 600 peak — is that across global routing, or per-region? We expect 60% of traffic from US, 30% EU, 10% APAC.
- Data residency: legal will want an explicit statement that inference for EU users stays on EU-hosted instances; please confirm how Redwood enforces residency (KMS separation, routing policies, and audit logs).

Also — can you share the perf matrix in CSV? Our infra team prefers to load it directly.

Great questions — answers below and attached a CSV export of the matrix.  TL;DR: we can meet the targets with a regional routing policy + per-tenant residency pinning; POC will show end-to-end.

- Streaming warm vs cold: warm sessions (cached KV / warmed model host) sustain ~45–60 tokens/sec; cold starts drop to ~8–12 tokens/sec for the first 1–2 seconds while KV cache is filled.  We recommend a short pre-warm (1–2 token primes) for interactive flows.
- Concurrency: the 200 steady / 600 peak is global. For your traffic split (60/30/10) that maps roughly to US: 120 steady / 360 peak, EU: 60 steady / 180 peak, APAC: 20 steady / 60 peak.  We'll size Dedicated pools accordingly and propose burst capacity.
- Data residency enforcement: we enforce region pins at the control plane and runtime routing layer; EU tenancy can be configured to never route inference to non-EU hosts. KMS keys are region-scoped (we integrate with customer KMS via HSM-backed keys for Private deployments). Audit logs show per-request region and model host id. I'll link the runbook in the attached CSV row 4.

Attached: performance-matrix.csv, SOC2-questions.pdf.

Action: can you share a ~24 hour anonymized traffic dump and two representative prompt templates? If yes, Marcus & Karthik will provision a small Dedicated pool for the POC and return sizing within 48 hours.

—
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
